sentences.text: If any of the encroachers fail to comply with the direction within 30 days, the Deputy Commissioner and other concerned authorities would be free to remove the encroachment in accordance with law.

iv) If the properties are found to be absolutely belonging to petitioners and not an encroachment, then the State and the authorities shall proceed in accordance with law to acquire the land by specifying the extent of area required for widening the road and by paying compensation to the petitioners as per law.

2. The grievance of the complainants in the present contempt petition is that the accused have not complied the direction Nos.(iii) and (iv) stated supra, thereby they have approached this Court by filing the present contempt petition on 23rd July 2018.

This Court passed several orders and ultimately, the compliance affidavit filed by the accused.
3. The order dated 3rd January 2023 passed in the present contempt petition in respect of direction No.(iv) reads as under:
"This is an unfortunate case where the learned Single Judge of this Court as long back as on 2nd December, 2016 had disposed of Writ Petition No.44815-826/2016 and connected matters by issuing four directions and now the grievance of the complainants is only with regard to Direction No.4 which has not been complied with and the same reads as under:
"iv) If the properties are found to be absolutely belonging to petitioners and not an encroachment, then the State and the authorities shall proceed in accordance with law to acquire the land by specifying the extent of area required for widening the road and by paying compensation to the petitioners as per law."

In response to the notice issued by this Court in the present contempt petition, the accused have filed as many as seven affidavits, but none of the affidavits disclose correctly the land acquired, the extent of area required for widening of the road, compensation claimed and even though the annexures are produced, this Court is not happy with the way in which the authorities have filed the affidavits, when they are contemplated to file in proper manner.

Hence, in the absence of mentioning the specific area required for widening of the road, mere filing affidavits and annexures for awarding revised compensation would not resolve the dispute between the parties and unnecessarily from the year 2016 till 2023, the authorities have dragged the matter.

sentences.text: In view of the above, as a last chance, finally one week's time is granted to the accused to file proper affidavit with regard to compliance of the order passed by this Court, failing which, the accused shall be present before the Court on the next day of hearing to hear and frame the charges against them.

4. The order dated 17th January 2023 passed in the present contempt petition reads as under:
"Inspite of the repeated orders passed by this Court in the present contempt petition,
the accused has not complied the direction No.(iv) issued by the learned Single Judge, which reads as under:
"iv) If the properties are found to be absolutely belonging to petitioners and not an encroachment, then the State and the authorities shall proceed in accordance with law to acquire the land by specifying the extent of area required for widening the road and by paying compensation to the petitioners as per law."

Sri M.D. Raghunath, learned counsel for the complainants invited the attention of the Court to paragraph 4(a) of the affidavit filed by the Deputy Commissioner dated 12.1.2023, wherein it is stated that the land of the complainant No.1 utilized for the purpose of formation of road is 32.94 square meters + 28.79 square meters and the total amount of compensation determined at the highest market value existing as on the year 2021 paid to the complainant for the acquisition of the aforementioned land is Rs.18,42,888/- (inclusive of previously awarded compensation amount Rs.10,17,717/-).
A copy of the revised award amount dated 3.7.2021 is produced at Anenxure-R1 of the affidavit.

However, as per Annexure-R8 produced along with the affidavit, in respect of the same 1st complainant, it is stated that the land utilized for the road is 13.71 x 4.50 = 61.70 square meters and that the building utilized for the road is 13.71 x 2.10 = 28.79 square meters.

Therefore, Annexure-R1 and Annexure-R8 in respect of the - 10 - complainant No.1 are not tallying, thereby it clearly indicates that the State Government by filing the affidavit of the Deputy Commissioner, has not come to the Court with clean hands and appraised the Court in the proper way.
At this stage, learned HCGP seeks time.
Post this matter next week.

In the mean time, learned counsel for the complainants shall furnish details relating to what is the correct extent of land acquired in terms of the order of the learned Single Judge and what is the compensation paid in respect of all the seven complainants in the present contempt petition."

Sri Raghunath, learned counsel for the complainants would contend that direction Nos.(iii) and (v) issued by this Court clearly depict that if any of the petitioners are found to be encroachers of public road or public property, they shall be given 30 days time to remove the encroached portion by specifying the same, on their own.

If any of the encroachers fail to comply with the direction within 30 days, the Deputy Commissioner and other concerned authorities would be free to - 19 - remove the encroachment in accordance with law.

If the properties are found to be absolutely belonging to petitioners and not an encroachment, then the State and the authorities shall proceed in accordance with law to acquire the land by specifying the extent of area required for widening the road and by paying compensation to the petitioners as per law.

Learned counsel for the complainants would contend that there was dispute with regard to the extent of area acquired for widening the road in respect of complainant Nos.1 to 4, thereby the accused have not paid the compensation fully with regard to demolition of the property.

He would further contend that insofar as complainant Nos.5 to 7, they have been paid compensation for removal of the structure, but not paid compensation for land, thereby he submits that the authorities have not complied the order in its entirety.

7. Sri Kiran Kumar, learned HCGP while reiterating the averments made in the compliance affidavit dated 22nd February 2023 would contend that there was dispute between the complainants and the State with regard to extent of land utilized for formation of the road.

As per the said survey,

Therefore, learned HCGP would contend that the order passed by the learned Single Judge has been complied.

8. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for the parties, the only point that would arise for our consideration in the present contempt petition, is:
"Whether the complainants have made out a case to proceed further to initiate contempt proceedings against the accused persons in the facts and circumstances of the case ?"
9.

Having considered the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for the parties, it is not in dispute that the learned Single Judge of this Court while disposing of the writ petitions by the order dated 2nd December 2016, has given four directions as stated supra.
The said order has reached finality.

It is also not in dispute that after several orders passed by this Court, ultimately the authorities now realized and conducted survey in presence of the complainants on the basis of the title deeds of the complainants, who attested their signatures on the spot mahazar conducted at the time of survey.

As per the said survey, insofar as complainant Nos.1 and 2, they have been paid compensation towards land lost and also for the building as - 22 - stated in paragraph-8(a) and 8(b) of the compliance affidavit.

However, on humanitarian grounds and as per the order passed by this Court in CCC No.1803/2017 dated 26.3.2018, the compensation was paid towards the houses of complainant Nos.5 to 7 and compensation amount paid is Rs.8,50,116/-,
Rs.4,38,166/- and Rs.89,018/- respectively.

10. Though learned counsel for the complainants would contend that inspite of the order of the Deputy Commissioner dated 13.9.2021 to pay compensation to complainant Nos.5 to 7 in respect of the land also, the authorities have paid the compensation only to the houses and not for the land.
Further, complainant Nos.1 to 7 are not happy with compensation paid.
It is for complainant Nos.1 to 7 to approach the Deputy Commissioner and all the concerned authorities for the grievance, if any in accordance with law.

For the reasons stated above, we answer the point raised in the present contempt petition in the negative holding that the complainants have not made out a case to proceed further to initiate contempt proceedings against the accused persons in the facts and circumstances of the case.

12. In view of the above, we pass the following:
ORDER i) The contempt proceedings are hereby dropped.
ii) However, it is needless to observe that it is always open for complainant Nos.1 to 7 to approach the Deputy Commissioner and all the concerned authorities for the grievance, if any in accordance with law.
iii) In respect of complainant Nos.3 and 4, the State has undertaken to pay the compensation for the additional extent of lands as stated in paragraphs- 8(c) and 8(d) of the affidavit dated 22.2.2023.

The same shall be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of copy of the order,
failing which complainant Nos.3 and 4 are - 24 - entitled to future interest at 9% for one year and thereafter at 15% as per the Land Acquisition Act.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The complainants have filed the present contempt petition to take action against the accused under the provisions of Sections 11 and 12 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 for willful and deliberate disobedience of the order dated 2nd December, 2016 made in Writ Petition Nos.44815-826/2016 and connected matters, wherein the learned Single Judge of this Court while disposing of the said writ petitions, has issued the following directions:
i) Petitioners shall file statement of objections along with necessary documents Sri C K Kumaraswamy vs Sri D S Ramesh on 14 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158545039/
4 before the Deputy Commissioner, Chamarajnagar, within two weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order;
ii) The Deputy Commissioner shall consider the objections and hear them by providing personal hearing to the petitioners and thereafter, pass a considered order;
iii) If any of the petitioners are found to be encroachers of public road or public property, they shall be given 30 days time to remove the encroached portion by specifying the same, on their own.
If any of the encroachers fail to comply with the direction within 30 days, the Deputy Commissioner and other concerned authorities would be free to remove the encroachment in accordance with law.
This Court passed several orders and ultimately, the compliance affidavit filed by the accused.
3. The order dated 3rd January 2023 passed in the present contempt petition in respect of direction No.(iv) reads as under:
"This is an unfortunate case where the learned Single Judge of this Court as long back as on 2nd December, 2016 had disposed of Writ Petition No.44815-826/2016 and connected matters by issuing four directions and now the grievance of the complainants is only with regard to Direction No.4 which has not been complied with and the same reads as under:
"iv) If the properties are found to be absolutely belonging to petitioners and not an encroachment, then the State and the authorities shall proceed in accordance with law to acquire the land by specifying the extent of area required for widening the road and by paying compensation to the petitioners as per law."
In response to the notice issued by this Court in the present contempt petition, the accused have filed as many as seven affidavits, but none of the affidavits disclose correctly the land acquired, the extent of area required for widening of the road, compensation claimed and even though the annexures are produced, this Court is not happy with the way in which the authorities have filed the affidavits, when they are contemplated to file in proper manner.
Hence, in the absence of mentioning the specific area required for widening of the road, mere filing affidavits and annexures for awarding revised compensation would not resolve the dispute between the parties and unnecessarily from the year 2016 till 2023, the authorities have dragged the matter.
4. The order dated 17th January 2023 passed in the present contempt petition reads as under:
"Inspite of the repeated orders passed by this Court in the present contempt petition,
the accused has not complied the direction No.(iv) issued by the learned Single Judge, which reads as under:
"iv) If the properties are found to be absolutely belonging to petitioners and not an encroachment, then the State and the authorities shall proceed in accordance with law to acquire the land by specifying the extent of area required for widening the road and by paying compensation to the petitioners as per law."
As such the State has to now pay compensation for the additional extent of lands which is to an extent of 3.9 sq.mts.
The said complainant was not paid the value of the land since he was found to be in unauthorised occupation of the lands in question.
The said complainant was not paid the value of the land since he was found to be in Sri C K Kumaraswamy vs Sri D S Ramesh on 14 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158545039/
9 unauthorised occupation of the lands in question.
In respect of the actual extent of land utilized by the State for the purpose of formation of the road,
the State accepted the latest survey conducted by the Executive Engineer.
In respect of complainant Nos.5 to 7, they were found to be in unauthorised occupation of the lands in question and hence they were not paid the value of the land.
However, on humanitarian grounds and as per the order passed by this Court in CCC No.1803/2017 dated 26.3.2018, the compensation was paid towards the houses of the complainant Nos.5 to 7 and total compensation amount paid is Rs.8,50,116/-, Rs.4,38,166/-
and Rs.89,018/- respectively.

In the mean time, learned counsel for the complainants shall furnish details relating to what is the correct extent of land acquired in terms of the order of the learned Single Judge and what is the compensation paid in respect of all the seven complainants in the present contempt petition."
The compensation which is already paid for the purpose of building is Rs.2,73,624/-.

(c) In respect of the Complainant No.3 is concerned, the actual extent of land which is utilized for the purpose of widening of road is 123.31 sq.mtr, as per the report of Executive Engineer, Public Works Department.
The compensation which is already paid for the purpose of building is Rs. NIL.
The Copy of the order dated: 03.07.2021 for having paid compensation on earlier occasions to an 82.74 sq.mtrs., extent of land is produced herewith ANNEXURE-R7.
In respect of complainant Nos.3 and 4, the State has undertaken to pay the compensation for the additional extent of lands as stated in paragraphs-8(c) and 8(d) of the affidavit.
However, on humanitarian grounds and as per the order passed by this Court in CCC No.1803/2017 dated 26.3.2018, the compensation was paid towards the houses of complainant Nos.5 to 7 and compensation amount paid is Rs.8,50,116/-,
Rs.4,38,166/- and Rs.89,018/- respectively.
Further, complainant Nos.1 to 7 are not happy with compensation paid.
It is for complainant Nos.1 to 7 to approach the Deputy Commissioner and all the concerned authorities for the grievance, if any in accordance with law.

ORDER i) The contempt proceedings are hereby dropped.

The same shall be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of copy of the order,

In respect of complainant Nos.5 to 7, they were found to be in unauthorised occupation of the lands in question and hence they were not paid the value of the land.
For the reasons stated above, we answer the point raised in the present contempt petition in the negative holding that the complainants have not made out a case to proceed further to initiate contempt proceedings against the accused persons in the facts and circumstances of the case.
